note: Setup lines for path cards, keyed by route id. Each says who travels and why, so a path card makes sense on its own. The card shows it above the route's text. A key with no matching route stops the build.

intros.genesis-16-hagar-flees: Hagar is Sarai's Egyptian servant. Sarai has no child, so she gives Hagar to Abram as a wife, and Hagar conceives.
intros.genesis-32-mahanaim-penuel: After twenty years with his uncle Laban, Jacob is going home to Canaan. He fears meeting his brother Esau, whose blessing he took.
intros.genesis-42-brothers-egypt: A famine covers Canaan, and only Egypt has grain. The brothers do not know that Joseph, whom they sold as a slave, now governs Egypt.
intros.genesis-45-brothers-return: Joseph has told his brothers who he is. He sends them home to bring their father, Jacob, down to Egypt for the rest of the famine.
intros.exodus-3-flock-horeb: Moses grew up in Pharaoh's house but fled Egypt after killing an Egyptian. In Midian he married a daughter of Jethro, a priest, and now tends his flocks.
intros.exodus-14-turn-to-sea: After the tenth plague, Pharaoh lets Israel go. Moses leads them out of Egypt, and God goes before them in a pillar of cloud and fire.
intros.exodus-15-sea-elim: Israel has crossed the Red Sea and left Egypt behind. Moses leads them into the wilderness toward Mount Sinai.
intros.exodus-16-elim-sin: Israel is a month out of Egypt, travelling under Moses toward Mount Sinai. Here the people complain of hunger, and God sends manna.
intros.exodus-17-sin-rephidim: Israel travels under Moses toward Mount Sinai. At Rephidim the people quarrel for water, and the Amalekites attack.
intros.exodus-19-rephidim-sinai: Three months after leaving Egypt, Israel reaches Mount Sinai. There God will make a covenant with them and give the law.
intros.numbers-13-spies: Israel has left Sinai and camps in the wilderness of Paran, south of Canaan. Moses sends one leader from each tribe to scout the land God promised.
intros.numbers-20-edom-request: Near the end of the forty years in the wilderness, Israel sets out from Kadesh toward Canaan. The direct way runs through Edom, the land of Esau's descendants.
intros.numbers-21-around-edom: Edom has refused to let Israel pass, so Moses leads the people the long way around it toward the Jordan and Canaan.
intros.numbers-21-sihon-og: Israel asks the Amorite king Sihon for passage through his land on the way to the Jordan, promising to keep to the king's highway.
intros.deuteronomy-34-moab-nebo: Moses is 120 years old. God has said he will see the promised land but not enter it, and Joshua will lead Israel across the Jordan.
intros.joshua-2-spies-jericho: Moses has died, and Joshua now leads Israel. They camp east of the Jordan, and Jericho is the first city in their way into Canaan.
intros.joshua-7-jericho-ai: Jericho has fallen. God ordered its plunder destroyed, but Achan secretly kept some, and Israel does not yet know it.
intros.joshua-8-ai-ebal: Achan's sin has been dealt with, and Israel now takes Ai. Moses had commanded an altar and a reading of the law at Mount Ebal once they entered the land.
intros.joshua-9-gibeon-gilgal: Israel's victories at Jericho and Ai have frightened the cities of Canaan. Gibeon is close by and fears it will be next.
intros.judges-7-midian-flees: The Midianites have raided Israel's crops for seven years. Gideon attacks their camp at night with three hundred men carrying trumpets and torches in jars.
intros.judges-9-to-thebez: Abimelech, a son of Gideon, killed seventy of his brothers to rule Shechem. Now Shechem has turned against him.
intros.judges-11-against-ammon: The Ammonites are oppressing Gilead. Its elders bring back Jephthah, a warrior his brothers had driven out, to lead them.
intros.judges-14-down-to-timnah: Samson, of the tribe of Dan, has been set apart to God as a Nazirite from birth. The Philistines rule over Israel.
intros.judges-14-to-ashkelon: At his wedding feast in Timnah, Samson bet thirty Philistine guests thirty sets of clothes on a riddle. They forced the answer out of his bride.
intros.judges-16-gaza-gates: Samson visits the Philistine city of Gaza. Its men surround the gate and wait to kill him at dawn.
intros.judges-16-sorek-gaza: Samson has fought the Philistines for twenty years. Their lords pay Delilah to learn the secret of his strength.
intros.judges-20-mizpah-gibeah: Men of Gibeah, in Benjamin, abused and killed a Levite's concubine. He sent pieces of her body to every tribe, calling Israel to act.
intros.judges-20-rimmon-flight: Benjamin refuses to hand over the men of Gibeah, so the other tribes go to war against it.
intros.judges-21-jabesh-shiloh: Benjamin is almost destroyed, and the tribes swore not to give it their daughters as wives. Now they fear the tribe will die out.
intros.1-samuel-13-gilgal-gibeah: Saul is Israel's first king. Facing the Philistines, he waited seven days at Gilgal for Samuel, then offered the sacrifice himself.
intros.1-samuel-15-carmel-gilgal: God sends Saul to destroy the Amalekites completely. Saul wins, but he spares King Agag and the best of the livestock.
intros.1-samuel-28-saul-endor: Samuel has died, and God no longer answers Saul. The Philistines gather for war, and Saul is afraid.
intros.2-samuel-4-head-to-hebron: After Saul's death, David reigns over Judah at Hebron. Saul's son Ishbosheth rules the other tribes, and the two houses are at war.
intros.2-samuel-10-envoys-rabbah: Nahash, king of Ammon, had been kind to David, and has died. His son Hanun's advisers say David's men are spies.
intros.2-samuel-11-uriah-letter: While his army besieges Rabbah, David has taken Bathsheba, and she is pregnant. Her husband, Uriah, is one of David's soldiers.
intros.2-samuel-12-david-rabbah: Rabbah is the Ammonite capital. Joab has besieged it since the war with Ammon began.
intros.2-samuel-14-absalom-returns: David's son Absalom killed his brother Amnon for raping their sister Tamar. He fled to his grandfather in Geshur and has stayed there three years.
intros.2-samuel-24-census-circuit: David orders a count of Israel's fighting men. Joab objects, and later David confesses the census was a sin.
intros.1-kings-3-solomon-gibeon: David has died, and his son Solomon is the new king. The temple is not yet built, so the people worship at high places.
intros.1-kings-15-asa-damascus: Asa is king of Judah. Baasha, king of Israel, is fortifying Ramah, just north of Jerusalem, to cut off Judah's road.
intros.1-kings-16-omri-samaria: Omri, an army commander, became king of Israel after a civil war. Tirzah had been the northern kingdom's capital.
intros.2-kings-1-ekron-messengers: Ahaziah, son of Ahab, is king of Israel. He has fallen through a lattice in his upper room in Samaria and lies badly hurt.
intros.2-kings-4-shunem-carmel: The Shunammite woman had given Elisha a room in her house. He promised her a son, and the boy was born.
intros.2-kings-6-dothan-samaria: The king of Aram is at war with Israel. Elisha keeps warning Israel's king where Aram's army will strike.
intros.2-kings-10-jehu-samaria: Elisha had Jehu anointed king of Israel to destroy the house of Ahab. Jehu has already killed King Joram and Jezebel at Jezreel.
intros.2-kings-12-hazael-jerusalem: Joash is king of Judah. Hazael, king of Aram, is raiding Israel and Judah.
intros.2-kings-15-north-exiled: Pekah is king of Israel. Assyria is the great empire of the day, and its king, Tiglath Pileser, invades from the north.
intros.2-kings-17-samaria-exiled: Hoshea, Israel's last king, served Assyria but stopped paying tribute and asked Egypt for help.
intros.2-kings-18-lachish-jerusalem: Hezekiah, king of Judah, rebelled against Assyria. Sennacherib of Assyria has invaded Judah and is besieging Lachish.
intros.2-kings-20-babylon-envoys: Hezekiah, king of Judah, has recovered from a deadly illness. The king of Babylon hears of it and sends envoys.
intros.2-kings-23-josiah-megiddo: Josiah, king of Judah, has led a great reform and renewed the covenant. Pharaoh Necoh is marching north to help Assyria.
intros.2-kings-23-jehoahaz-egypt: Josiah has died at Megiddo, and the people made his son Jehoahaz king. He reigns only three months.
intros.1-chronicles-10-jabesh-rescue: Saul and his sons have died fighting the Philistines on Mount Gilboa. Saul once rescued Jabesh Gilead from the Ammonites.
intros.1-chronicles-11-to-jerusalem: Saul is dead, and all Israel accepts David as king. Jerusalem is still held by the Jebusites.
intros.1-chronicles-11-bethlehem-well: David is at the cave of Adullam, and a Philistine garrison holds his hometown, Bethlehem. The three men are among his mighty men.
intros.1-chronicles-13-ark-first-try: David is king in Jerusalem. The ark of the covenant has stayed at Kiriath Jearim since the Philistines sent it back, years before.
intros.1-chronicles-14-gibeon-gezer: The Philistines hear that David has been anointed king over all Israel, and they come up to attack.
intros.1-chronicles-19-envoys-rabbah: Nahash, king of Ammon, had been kind to David, and has died. His son Hanun's advisers say David's men are spies.
intros.1-chronicles-20-joab-rabbah: Rabbah is the Ammonite capital. The war began after Hanun shamed David's envoys.
intros.1-chronicles-21-census: Satan moves David to number Israel. Joab objects, and later David confesses the census was a sin.
intros.2-chronicles-1-solomon-gibeon: David has died, and his son Solomon is the new king. The tabernacle Moses made stands at Gibeon.
intros.2-chronicles-2-timber-rafts: Solomon is preparing to build the temple. Huram, king of Tyre, was his father David's friend.
intros.2-chronicles-9-sheba-visit: Solomon's fame for wisdom has spread far. Sheba was a kingdom in southern Arabia.
intros.2-chronicles-10-rehoboam-flees: Solomon has died. The northern tribes ask his son Rehoboam to lighten his father's heavy labor and taxes, and he refuses.
intros.2-chronicles-12-shishak: Rehoboam is king of Judah. Once his kingdom is strong, he and the people forsake the law of the LORD.
intros.2-chronicles-14-zerah-pursuit: Asa, king of Judah, has removed the idols and fortified his cities. The land has had ten years of peace.
intros.2-chronicles-16-asa-damascus: Asa is king of Judah. Baasha, king of Israel, is fortifying Ramah, just north of Jerusalem, to cut off Judah's road.
intros.2-chronicles-18-ramoth-campaign: Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, has made a marriage alliance with Ahab, king of Israel. Ahab wants to take Ramoth Gilead back from Aram.
intros.2-chronicles-20-to-tekoa: Moab, Ammon, and others invade Judah. King Jehoshaphat and the people fast and pray, and a Levite tells them the battle is God's.
intros.2-chronicles-25-amaziah-captured: Amaziah, king of Judah, has defeated Edom. Proud of the victory, he challenges Joash, king of Israel, to battle.
intros.2-chronicles-28-captives-samaria: Ahaz, king of Judah, worships other gods. Pekah, king of Israel, invades Judah and kills thousands in one day.
intros.2-chronicles-28-captives-jericho: Israel's army has carried thousands of Judah's people to Samaria as captives. They are their own kin.
intros.2-chronicles-30-passover-letters: Hezekiah, the new king of Judah, has cleansed the temple. He invites the northern tribes who escaped Assyria to keep the Passover in Jerusalem.
intros.2-chronicles-32-lachish-envoys: Hezekiah, king of Judah, rebelled against Assyria. Sennacherib of Assyria has invaded Judah and is besieging Lachish.
intros.2-chronicles-33-manasseh-taken: Manasseh, son of Hezekiah, has led Judah into idol worship and ignored the LORD's warnings.
intros.2-chronicles-33-manasseh-back: Manasseh, the idolatrous king of Judah, has been carried to Babylon in chains by Assyria's captains.
intros.2-chronicles-35-josiah-megiddo: Josiah, king of Judah, has repaired the temple and kept a great Passover. Pharaoh Neco is marching north to fight at the Euphrates.
intros.2-chronicles-36-exile: Judah's last kings ignore the prophets God sends. Babylon, under Nebuchadnezzar, now rules the region.
intros.2-chronicles-36-cyrus-call: Babylon has fallen to Persia. Jeremiah had said the exile would last seventy years.
intros.ezra-1-first-return: The Jews have lived in exile in Babylon since Nebuchadnezzar destroyed Jerusalem and its temple. Now Cyrus of Persia has conquered Babylon.
intros.ezra-2-register-return: Cyrus of Persia has let the exiles go home to Judah to rebuild the temple.
intros.ezra-3-cedar: The exiles have come home from Babylon and are rebuilding the temple Nebuchadnezzar destroyed.
intros.ezra-5-letter-to-darius: Urged on by the prophets Haggai and Zechariah, the Jews have started work on the temple again. Local officials question whether they have permission.
intros.ezra-7-ezra-journey: Ezra is a priest and scribe among the Jews still in Babylon, about sixty years after the temple was rebuilt. King Artaxerxes sends him to teach God's law in Judah.
intros.ezra-8-ahava-jerusalem: King Artaxerxes has sent Ezra, a priest and scribe, to teach God's law in Judah. Ezra is carrying gifts of silver and gold for the temple.
intros.nehemiah-2-susa-jerusalem: Nehemiah is cupbearer to the Persian king Artaxerxes at Susa. He has heard that Jerusalem's walls lie in ruins, and asks leave to rebuild them.
intros.nehemiah-13-second-return: Nehemiah governed Judah for twelve years and rebuilt Jerusalem's wall. Then he went back to the king.
intros.esther-2-mordecai-exile: The story is set at Susa under the Persian king Ahasuerus. Mordecai, a Jew, raised his young cousin Esther as his own daughter.
intros.aram-against-judah: Aram (Syria) and Israel want Judah to join them against Assyria. When King Ahaz refuses, they march on Jerusalem, and Isaiah tells him not to fear.
intros.israel-against-judah: Aram (Syria) and Israel want Judah to join them against Assyria. When King Ahaz refuses, they march on Jerusalem, and Isaiah tells him not to fear.
intros.assyria-damascus: Isaiah names his son as a sign: before the boy can talk, Assyria will plunder Damascus and Samaria, the two kingdoms threatening Judah.
intros.assyria-samaria: Isaiah names his son as a sign: before the boy can talk, Assyria will plunder Damascus and Samaria, the two kingdoms threatening Judah.
intros.assyria-jerusalem: Isaiah warns that because Judah rejects the LORD's help, Assyria will sweep over Judah like a flood, up to its neck.
intros.northern-approach: Isaiah warns that God will use Assyria to punish his people, then humble Assyria for its pride.
intros.gather-assyria: Isaiah foresees a day when the Lord sets his hand a second time to gather his scattered people home.
intros.gather-egypt: Isaiah foresees a day when the Lord sets his hand a second time to gather his scattered people home.
intros.gather-pathros: Isaiah foresees a day when the Lord sets his hand a second time to gather his scattered people home.
intros.gather-cush: Isaiah foresees a day when the Lord sets his hand a second time to gather his scattered people home.
intros.gather-elam: Isaiah foresees a day when the Lord sets his hand a second time to gather his scattered people home.
intros.gather-babylon: Isaiah foresees a day when the Lord sets his hand a second time to gather his scattered people home.
intros.gather-hamath: Isaiah foresees a day when the Lord sets his hand a second time to gather his scattered people home.
intros.medes-babylon: Isaiah prophesies the fall of Babylon, the proud empire that will one day carry Judah into exile.
intros.moab-flight-zoar: Isaiah laments over Moab, Israel's neighbor east of the Dead Sea, as disaster falls on it in a single night.
intros.moab-flight-luhith: Isaiah laments over Moab, Israel's neighbor east of the Dead Sea, as disaster falls on it in a single night.
intros.moab-flight-horonaim: Isaiah laments over Moab, Israel's neighbor east of the Dead Sea, as disaster falls on it in a single night.
intros.moab-flight-brook-of-the-willows: Isaiah laments over Moab, Israel's neighbor east of the Dead Sea, as disaster falls on it in a single night.
intros.moab-arnon: Isaiah's oracle on Moab continues. Moab's refugees seek shelter, and Moab is told to take refuge with Judah.
intros.sela-zion: Isaiah's oracle on Moab continues. Moab is told to send tribute to Judah's ruler and seek shelter there.
intros.egypt-assyria-highway: Isaiah foresees a day when Egypt and Assyria, Israel's two great enemies, worship the LORD together with Israel.
intros.assyria-ashdod: The Philistine city of Ashdod has rebelled against Assyria, hoping Egypt and Cush will help. Isaiah walks stripped and barefoot as a warning.
intros.captivity-egypt: Isaiah walks stripped and barefoot for three years as a sign. Egypt and Cush, whom Judah hopes will save it from Assyria, will themselves be led away captive.
intros.captivity-cush: Isaiah walks stripped and barefoot for three years as a sign. Egypt and Cush, whom Judah hopes will save it from Assyria, will themselves be led away captive.
intros.arabian-refuge: Isaiah's oracle on Arabia foresees war reaching the desert tribes and their trading caravans.
intros.sidon-kittim: Isaiah prophesies against Tyre and Sidon, the rich trading ports of Phoenicia. Their trade will end, and their people will flee.
intros.return-assyria: Isaiah foresees a great trumpet calling home the scattered exiles to worship the LORD in Jerusalem.
intros.return-egypt: Isaiah foresees a great trumpet calling home the scattered exiles to worship the LORD in Jerusalem.
intros.egypt-envoys: Judah's leaders send envoys to seek an alliance with Egypt against Assyria. Isaiah warns that Egypt's help is worthless.
intros.judah-campaign: Hezekiah, king of Judah, has rebelled against Assyria. King Sennacherib invades Judah and takes its walled towns.
intros.lachish-mission: Hezekiah, king of Judah, has rebelled against Assyria. King Sennacherib invades and sends his field commander to demand Jerusalem's surrender.
intros.west-campaign: Hezekiah, king of Judah, has rebelled against Assyria with other kings of the coast. King Sennacherib marches west to crush the revolt.
intros.philistine-campaign: Hezekiah, king of Judah, has rebelled against Assyria with other kings of the coast. King Sennacherib marches west to crush the revolt.
intros.lachish-libnah: Sennacherib's field commander has demanded Jerusalem's surrender. Hezekiah turns to Isaiah, who says the Assyrian king will go home.
intros.return-nineveh: Hezekiah prayed for deliverance, and Isaiah said Sennacherib would not enter Jerusalem. That night an angel strikes the Assyrian camp.
intros.babylon-envoys-route: Hezekiah, king of Judah, has recovered from a deadly illness. The king of Babylon sends envoys, and Hezekiah shows them all his treasures.
intros.future-exile: Hezekiah has shown Babylon's envoys all his treasures. Isaiah warns that one day everything will be carried to Babylon.
intros.return-babylon: Isaiah speaks to the future exiles in Babylon, promising that the LORD will redeem them.
intros.gifts-midian: Isaiah sees Zion's future glory, when the nations come to its light and bring their wealth to Jerusalem.
intros.gifts-sheba: Isaiah sees Zion's future glory, when the nations come to its light and bring their wealth to Jerusalem.
intros.gifts-kedar: Isaiah sees Zion's future glory, when the nations come to its light and bring their wealth to Jerusalem.
intros.nations-javan: In Isaiah's closing vision, the Lord gathers all nations to see his glory, and sends messengers to distant lands.
intros.nations-lud: In Isaiah's closing vision, the Lord gathers all nations to see his glory, and sends messengers to distant lands.
intros.nations-tubal: In Isaiah's closing vision, the Lord gathers all nations to see his glory, and sends messengers to distant lands.
intros.jeremiah-24-jeconiah-exile: Jeremiah prophesies in Jerusalem in Judah's last years. Babylon has besieged the city, and the young king surrenders.
intros.jeremiah-26-uriah-egypt: Jeremiah has warned that the temple will be destroyed. King Jehoiakim punishes prophets who say such things.
intros.jeremiah-37-pharaoh-army: Babylon is besieging Jerusalem under King Zedekiah, who hopes Egypt will save the city.
intros.jeremiah-41-mizpah-captives: Babylon has destroyed Jerusalem and made Gedaliah governor at Mizpah. Ishmael, of the royal family, has murdered him.
intros.jeremiah-41-to-bethlehem: Ishmael murdered Gedaliah, Babylon's governor. Johanan has rescued his captives but fears Babylon will take revenge.
intros.jeremiah-43-to-tahpanhes: After Gedaliah's murder, the survivors asked Jeremiah what God wanted. He said to stay in Judah, but they refused.
intros.jeremiah-46-necoh-carchemish: Egypt and Babylon are fighting for control of the region after Assyria's fall.
intros.ezekiel-8-vision-jerusalem: Ezekiel is a priest exiled to Babylon with King Jehoiachin. Jerusalem still stands, and Judah's elders sit before him.
intros.ezekiel-17-king-taken: Ezekiel tells a riddle of two eagles and a vine. It pictures Judah's kings caught between Babylon and Egypt.
intros.ezekiel-17-envoys-egypt: Ezekiel's riddle of the eagles continues. Zedekiah swore loyalty to Babylon but now turns to Egypt.
intros.ezekiel-19-lion-egypt: Ezekiel sings a lament for the princes of Judah, whose last kings were taken captive.
intros.ezekiel-19-lion-babylon: Ezekiel sings a lament for the princes of Judah, whose last kings were taken captive.
intros.ezekiel-21-two-ways: Ezekiel, in exile, foresees Babylon's king marching against the rebels in Jerusalem and Ammon.
intros.ezekiel-26-against-tyre: Tyre, the rich port city, rejoiced when Jerusalem fell. Ezekiel prophesies its destruction.
intros.ezekiel-30-against-egypt: Judah trusted Egypt to protect it from Babylon. Ezekiel prophesies against Egypt.
intros.ezekiel-33-fugitive: Ezekiel has been in exile in Babylon for twelve years, warning that Jerusalem would fall.
intros.daniel-1-first-captives: Babylon takes its first captives from Jerusalem. Daniel and his three friends are among the young nobles chosen to serve the king.
intros.zechariah-6-exiles-arrive: Zechariah prophesies in Jerusalem as the exiles who returned from Babylon rebuild the temple.
intros.luke-10-jericho-road: A lawyer asks Jesus who his neighbor is. Jesus answers with the parable of the good Samaritan.
intros.acts-8-philip-samaria: Stephen has been stoned in Jerusalem, and Saul is leading a persecution of the church. Philip was one of the seven chosen to serve the believers.
intros.acts-8-gaza-road: Philip, one of the seven, has been preaching in Samaria. The Ethiopian official, treasurer to his queen, is going home from worship in Jerusalem.
intros.acts-8-philip-coast: Philip has just baptized the Ethiopian official on the Gaza road. Then the Spirit takes him away.
intros.acts-9-saul-damascus: Saul, a Pharisee, is arresting followers of Jesus. He sets out to bring any he finds in Damascus back to Jerusalem in chains.
intros.acts-9-saul-escape: Saul, now a believer, has been preaching in Damascus that Jesus is the Son of God. The Jews there plot to kill him.
intros.acts-10-cornelius-men: Cornelius is a Roman centurion at Caesarea, a Gentile who prays to God. An angel has told him to send for Peter.
intros.acts-10-peter-caesarea: In a vision God has taught Peter to call no one unclean. Messengers from Cornelius, a Gentile centurion, have come for him.
intros.acts-13-cyprus-pisidia: The church at Antioch is told by the Holy Spirit to set apart Barnabas and Saul. This is Paul's first mission.
intros.acts-15-council-trip: Some teachers from Judea are telling Gentile converts in Antioch that they must be circumcised to be saved.
intros.acts-15-council-letter: The council at Jerusalem has decided that Gentile converts need not be circumcised. Its letter tells the churches so.
intros.acts-16-to-macedonia: Paul and Silas set out on a second mission to visit the churches founded on the first.
intros.acts-17-macedonia-athens: On Paul's second mission he and Silas preach in Macedonia. In each city, opponents stir up crowds against them.
intros.acts-18-athens-corinth: On his second mission Paul has preached in Macedonia and at Athens.
intros.acts-18-sail-syria: Paul has spent a year and a half founding the church at Corinth. He heads home to Antioch, ending his second mission.
intros.acts-20-troas-miletus: Paul is ending his third mission. He is hurrying to reach Jerusalem by Pentecost with a gift for the poor saints there.
intros.acts-21-miletus-jerusalem: Paul is ending his third mission and going to Jerusalem with a gift for the poor saints, though he has been warned that chains await him.
intros.acts-23-paul-escort: Paul was arrested at the temple in Jerusalem. More than forty men have sworn to kill him, so the Roman commander sends him to the governor, Felix.
intros.acts-27-voyage-malta: Paul is a prisoner. He has appealed to Caesar, so the governor, Festus, sends him to Rome under a centurion named Julius. Luke and Aristarchus sail with him, and at Myra they board a ship of Alexandria bound for Italy.
intros.acts-28-malta-rome: Paul, a prisoner bound for trial before Caesar, was shipwrecked on Malta with everyone aboard. After three months the party sails on in another ship of Alexandria.
intros.revelation-1-seven-assemblies: John, the apostle, has been banished to the island of Patmos for his testimony of Jesus. The seven assemblies are churches in the Roman province of Asia.
intros.lehi-departs: Lehi is a prophet in Jerusalem shortly before Babylon destroys it. He warns the people, and they seek to kill him.
intros.plates-journey: The brass plates hold the scriptures and the record of Lehi's ancestors. Laban, a powerful man in Jerusalem, keeps them.
intros.ishmael-journey: Lehi's sons need wives to raise families in the promised land. Ishmael's family has daughters.
intros.valley-to-nahom: Lehi's family has camped in the valley of Lemuel. The Lord gives Lehi a brass ball, the Liahona, to point their way into the wilderness.
intros.nahom-to-bountiful: Lehi's family is crossing the Arabian wilderness, guided by the Liahona.
intros.lehi-arrival: At Bountiful the Lord showed Nephi how to build a ship. Lehi's family has sailed across the sea toward the promised land.
intros.nephi-separates: Lehi has died. Nephi's older brothers, Laman and Lemuel, are angry that he leads the family, and they seek to kill him.
intros.mulekite-arrival: Mulek was a son of Zedekiah, the last king of Judah. His group left Jerusalem about the time Babylon took the city.
intros.mulekites-up: Mulek, a son of Judah's last king, came with a group across the sea. Their descendants become the people of Zarahemla.
intros.mosiah-flight: Mosiah is a Nephite living in the land of Nephi, the Nephites' first home. The Lord warns him to flee with all who will listen.
intros.zeniff-return: Zeniff, a Nephite who once spied among the Lamanites, wants to reclaim the land of Nephi, the Nephites' first home.
intros.ammon-search: Zeniff led a group back to the land of Nephi long ago, and no word has come from them since. King Mosiah sends Ammon to find them.
intros.limhi-explorers: King Limhi's people, the descendants of Zeniff's group, are in bondage to the Lamanites. They seek Zarahemla to ask for help.
intros.alma-flees-noah: Alma, once a priest of wicked King Noah, believed the prophet Abinadi and baptized believers at the waters of Mormon. Noah sends his army against them.
intros.limhi-escape: Limhi's people are in bondage to the Lamanites. With Ammon's help, Gideon plans their escape by night.
intros.lost-lamanites: Limhi's people have escaped by night. The Lamanites send an army after them.
intros.alma-to-zarahemla: Alma's people are in bondage to Amulon, a former priest of King Noah, in the land of Helam. The Lord eases their burdens and promises to deliver them.
intros.amlicite-war: Amlici lost the people's vote to become king. His followers made him king anyway, and he leads them to war against the Nephites.
intros.alma-gideon: Alma has given up the judgment seat to preach repentance throughout the land.
intros.alma-circuit: Alma has given up the judgment seat to preach repentance throughout the land.
intros.ammonihah-attack: The people of Ammonihah rejected Alma and Amulek and burned the believers. Alma warned that the city would be destroyed.
intros.sons-of-mosiah: Ammon, Aaron, Omner, and Himni, sons of King Mosiah, once fought against the church. Now converted, they give up the throne to preach to the Lamanites.
intros.ammonites-to-jershon: Thousands of Lamanites converted by the sons of Mosiah buried their weapons. Other Lamanites are attacking them.
intros.ammonites-to-melek: The people of Ammon took in poor Zoramite converts, and the Zoramites prepare for war. The Nephite armies need Jershon.
intros.zerahemnah-roundabout: Zerahemnah leads Lamanites and Zoramites against the Nephites. Moroni, the young Nephite chief captain, has armed his men with armor.
intros.moroni-to-manti: Zerahemnah's army is moving to strike the land of Manti. Alma has learned by prophecy where it will go.
intros.morianton-flight: Morianton's people quarreled with the people of Lehi over land. To escape judgment, they flee toward the land northward.
intros.teancum-intercepts: Moroni fears that Morianton's people will take the land northward and threaten the Nephites' liberty.
intros.amalickiah-coast: Amalickiah, a Nephite dissenter, made himself king of the Lamanites by treachery. He leads them to war against the Nephites.
intros.mulek-decoy: The Lamanites hold the city of Mulek, which Amalickiah captured. Moroni plans to draw them out.
intros.helaman-to-judea: The people of Ammon swore never to fight again. Their two thousand sons covenant to defend the Nephites and choose Helaman to lead them.
intros.helaman-decoy: Helaman's two thousand young men are helping hold the Nephite cities in the west. The Lamanites in Antiparah will not come out to fight.
intros.moroni-retakes: Moroni has put down the king-men's rebellion in Zarahemla. He marches to end the long war with the Lamanites.
intros.hagoth-ships: After years of war, many Nephites are moving to the land northward. Hagoth is a shipbuilder.
intros.coriantumr-center: Zarahemla is divided by contention over the judgment seat, and its chief judge, Pahoran, has just been murdered.
intros.hel4-retreat: The Nephites have grown proud and wicked. Nephite dissenters stir up the Lamanites to war.
intros.nephi-lehi-preach: Nephi, son of Helaman, has given up the judgment seat to preach full time, with his brother Lehi.
intros.gather-south: The Gadianton robbers threaten to destroy the Nephites. Lachoneus, the governor, gathers everyone into one place to withstand them.
intros.gather-north: The Gadianton robbers threaten to destroy the Nephites. Lachoneus, the governor, gathers everyone into one place to withstand them.
intros.mormon-first-retreat: Mormon leads the Nephite armies though he is still young. The people are wicked, and the Lamanites are attacking.
intros.lamanites-north: The Nephites swore revenge for their dead, so Mormon refused to lead them. They attacked first and were driven back.
intros.mormon-final-retreat: Mormon takes command of the Nephite armies again, though he knows they will not repent.
intros.omer-flight: Omer is a Jaredite king. His son Jared has turned against him, and the Lord warns Omer in a dream to flee.
intros.jaredite-last-war: Coriantumr, the last Jaredite king, is at war with Shiz. The prophet Ether watches the destruction of his people.
